previous_description: A named monitoring dashboard that groups visualizations of APM signals (metrics, traces, logs) to provide operational visibility into system behavior. Represents the dashboard definition in the monitoring platform (e.g., Grafana, Datadog, CloudWatch), serving as the primary observability artifact teams consult during incidents and reviews.
definition: A persisted monitoring-platform view definition that arranges one or more visualization panels, each querying metrics, traces, logs or alert state, into a single named page for human inspection. It is the definition of the view (e.g., Grafana dashboard JSON, Datadog dashboard resource), not the underlying signals or the queries' alerting logic.

distinguish_from.when: the artifact evaluates a condition on a schedule and sends notifications, even if it is defined in the same platform or shown on a dashboard panel.
the code creates or records a measurement (Counter, Histogram, Gauge) rather than displaying or querying one.
the configuration sends telemetry to a backend (endpoint, protocol, auth) rather than defining how that backend visualizes it.

code_evidence: a Grafana dashboard JSON file (with 'panels', 'targets' and 'templating' keys) under a dashboards/ or provisioning/ directory, or a grafana-dashboard ConfigMap in Kubernetes manifests
an infrastructure-as-code resource such as Terraform 'datadog_dashboard', 'grafana_dashboard', 'aws_cloudwatch_dashboard' or 'newrelic_one_dashboard' containing widget definitions
a dashboard-as-code module (e.g., grafonnet/Jsonnet, grafanalib Python, CDK Dashboard construct) that builds panels with PromQL, LogQL or trace queries
notes: OpenTelemetry defines no dashboard concept, so standard_reference is null. Panels are an untyped array; consider a panel schema (title, query, visualization type, signal reference) so 'monitors' relationships can be derived. Enum lacks kibana, honeycomb, splunk, prometheus console. The 'monitors' relationship to apm.alert is semantically odd; 'displays' fits better.
